title: The understudy steps in
allegory: A backup name-mover head is like an understudy: while the lead delivers the key line it waits in the wings, but when the lead is knocked out it steps on and says the same line, so the show barely changes and a careless critic concludes the lead never mattered.

an understudy steps on and says the line
backups start moving the right name to the output
reviews say the show was nearly as good

chapters.name: The missing star
chapters.note: switched off the head that does the job ... and nothing broke?

cap.1: You switch off the part of the model that seems to do the job, expecting the answer to collapse. It barely changes. Was that part unimportant after all?
cap.2: In IOI, ablate the name mover heads that copy the right name to the output, and the logit difference falls far less than their contribution suggests.
cap.3: Ablation measures the total effect after the network re-routes. When other components compensate, the drop understates the ablated component's direct role.

cap.1: Think of a play. The lead calls in sick, an understudy steps in and says the same line, and the audience hardly notices. The lead still mattered.
cap.2: Backup name mover heads are understudies: they normally contribute little, but when the primary name movers are ablated they take over copying the right name.
cap.3: Wang et al. (arXiv:2211.00593) found backup name movers that take over when the primary movers 9.6, 9.9 and 10.0 are ablated: self-repair inside GPT-2 small.

cap.1: The line is said by a relay: early heads spot the repeated name, middle heads pass that on, late heads copy the other name out. Backups wait beside them.
cap.2: Name movers 9.6, 9.9 and 10.0 copy the indirect object; S-inhibition heads 7.3, 7.9, 8.6 and 8.10 steer them away from the repeated name. Backups sit alongside, mostly quiet.
cap.3: 26 heads in 7 classes, each validated causally. In DLA the backups sit between the strong positive name movers and the negative ones; they take over when the movers are ablated.

chapters.name: Hidden by cover
chapters.title: Push towards the right name, normal run then name movers ablated (illustrative)

cap.1: Before and after the lead leaves: the lead's share drops to nothing, the understudy's share grows, and the net only dips. The numbers are illustrative.
cap.2: Ablating the name movers removes their direct effect, but the backups raise theirs, so the net logit difference falls much less than the name movers' clean contribution.
cap.3: Total-effect drop = direct effect removed minus compensation added. A small total drop is compatible with a large direct effect. Values illustrative, not the paper's.

chapters.name: Reading an ablation
chapters.verdict: A small drop after ablation is not proof a part is unimportant.

cap.1: The trap: 'I removed it and nothing broke, so it does nothing.' With understudies around, that conclusion can be exactly wrong.
cap.2: Single-head ablation understates importance when backups exist. Pair it with direct logit attribution, and ablate groups of heads that might cover for each other.
cap.3: Report direct and total effects separately and use path patching to isolate routes. Compensation is itself a finding: the job is implemented redundantly.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: A small drop can hide a big role
Removing a part may not remove a skill

cap.1: Models can keep spare copies of important skills. When you test what a part does by removing it, remember the spares.
cap.2: Any time you knock out a component and see little change, ask whether something else took over before you call it unimportant.
cap.3: For steering and safety, 'we removed the circuit and the behaviour stayed' may mean backups rather than absence. Claims about what a model can no longer do need that check.

readouts.label: drop you measure at full ablation

caption.1: Left to right: ablate more of the lead heads. Orange is what you'd expect if nobody stepped in; teal is what you actually measure when understudies cover.
caption.2: Raise the backups' make-up and the measured drop shrinks, while the name movers' direct effect stays the same. At full cover, ablation shows nothing at all.
caption.3: Toy model: backups recover a fraction of the removed direct effect d. Measured drop = (1 - fraction)·d; d itself shows up only in DLA or path patching.

where_else: Any interpretability ablation study: report direct effects next to the drop
Safety claims like 'we removed the circuit, so the capability is gone', which backups can quietly falsify
Networks trained with dropout, which are pushed to spread one job across redundant units
Engineering with hot spares, where failover hides the primary's importance until both fail

hamming.what: Heads that take over the name-moving job in GPT-2 small's IOI circuit when the primary name movers are ablated.
hamming.when: Whenever you test a component's importance by removing it and the score barely moves.
hamming.why: Self-repair means a single ablation number is not evidence of unimportance, so claims about what a model needs, or can no longer do, must account for backups.

knobs.label: How much the understudies make up

cap.1: Three versions of the show: normal, lead heads out, and leads plus understudies out. Each bar is how hard a group pushes the right name.
cap.2: Rows are ablation conditions; columns are each group's direct push on the logit difference, plus the net. Heights illustrative.
cap.3: Direct effects per head class under three interventions; the net column is the total you would report.

cap.1: Middle row: with the leads out, the understudies' bar shoots up and the net barely dips.
cap.2: Ablating the primary movers: their bar goes to zero, backups compensate, net falls only a little.
cap.3: Total effect of ablating the movers is small because the backups' direct effect rises to replace theirs.

cap.1: If the understudies never stepped in, the net would crash. The gap between these two versions is what self-repair hides.
cap.2: With no compensation, the drop equals the movers' direct effect. That is the importance ablation failed to show.
cap.3: Setting compensation to 0 recovers the naive prediction: total effect equals direct effect.

cap.1: Back row: take the understudies out too and the net finally collapses. The job really did live in these heads.
cap.2: Ablating movers and backups together removes the cover and reveals the full dependence.
cap.3: Group ablation of redundant components exposes what single ablations mask.

cap.1: Full cover: the net is unchanged. An ablation score would call the leads useless, though they did most of the work.
cap.2: At complete compensation, single-head ablation reports zero importance for heads with the largest direct effect.
cap.3: Perfect self-repair makes the total effect vanish while the clean-run direct effect is unchanged.

predict.q: You ablate the name mover heads and the logit difference drops only a little. What can you conclude?

options.t: Not much yet: backups may be covering

predict.why: Self-repair: backup name movers take over, so single-head ablation understates importance.

predict.q: How could you reveal the name movers' real contribution?

options.t: Check their direct logit attribution, or ablate the backups too

predict.why: Direct effects show what they write in the normal run; removing the understudies removes the cover.

predict.q: In the normal run, how big is the backups' direct effect?
predict.why: In DLA they sit between the strong positive name movers and the negative ones, and grow when the movers are ablated.

object.where: Any system with spare capacity: removing one part understates its role whenever another part covers for it.
